canonical_project: AWS Falls Township/Keystone Trade Center campus
aliases: AWS Falls Township/Keystone Trade Center campus

location.address: 600 Ben Fairless Drive, Falls Township, Bucks County, PA

actions.summary: Falls Township reported approval of revised NorthPoint land development plans converting building six into a data center and shifting a 247-acre parcel from four distribution centers to 10 digital-infrastructure-campus structures totaling more than 2 million square feet.
Amazon announced at least $20 billion of Pennsylvania data-center investment, with Falls Township and Salem Township identified as the first communities for future innovation campuses.
DEP issued Air Quality Plan Approval 09-0261 to Amazon Data Services, Inc. for phase 1.
DEP issued Chapter 102 NPDES Permit PAD090088 A-3.

Amazon submitted phase 2 Plan Approval 09-0261A for 280 natural gas-fired critical backup generator engines and three diesel-fired ancillary emergency generator engines; DEP opened a 30-day public comment period starting July 18, 2026.

Falls Township described the Amazon data center as under construction, said Amazon had invested more than $827 million to date, reported 3 million square feet at completion, and said active construction would continue for two to three years.

capacity_note: Electrical IT load/capacity MW remains undisclosed in official sources; NorthPoint stated under NDA in March 2025 that the MW amount was significant but did not disclose it.
owner: Amazon Data Services, Inc. (facility permittee/operator); NorthPoint Development (owner/developer of Keystone Trade Center site)

contradictions.summary: Falls Township's June 2025 article describes building six as located at 1 Ben Fairless Drive, while DEP's 2026 page and proposed plan approval identify the Amazon Data Services facility at 600 Ben Fairless Drive / Morrisville, PA. Treat 600 Ben Fairless Drive as the current permitting address and retain the older township address as context.

Falls Township's March/June 2025 approval coverage described more than 2 million square feet across 10 digital-infrastructure structures on a 247-acre parcel; its July 2026 town-hall follow-up reported the site will be 3 million square feet once complete. This appears to reflect later buildout scope but was not reconciled in a site-plan document found during this refresh.
